descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-94513 AC 8, AC 9; TFA-94700 AC 2 · “A centrally revoked session is immediately unusable”. Mixed: stated part — A second device does not sign the first out; Sign out ends the session; an operator revoke makes the session unusable at once; our part — Sign out everywhere, and the sessions_revoked / signed_out audit rows (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S09 Ways a session ends, on screen and at the very next call: second device, Sign out, Sign out everywhere, operator revoke

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T2 Each device signs in with its own email OTP, and a new device always needs one. Phone and computer hold separate sessions that are valid at the same time: signing in on one never signs the other out. (TFA-94513 AC 6; TFA-94513 AC 9; TFA-94513 AC 10) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U9 Disabling a physician turns their access off immediately on every device, even without a separate revoke call. Disabling and revoking signs them out immediately, and they cannot request a new code. … (UAT OAT-01 step 9; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 8; TFA-94513 AC 14) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given A brand-new account with a phone session (API client) and a browser session (real sign-in form); fresh accounts with two API sessions each

When (a) Sign in on the browser while the phone is signed in. (b) Sign out in Settings. (c) Sign in again, then Sign out everywhere. (d) A fresh account's sessions are revoked by an operator while the tab is open, then the tab becomes visible. (e) Over the API: the operator revokes by email; …

Then (a) The phone stays signed in. (b) The browser is on the sign-in screen and the phone is still signed in. (c) The browser is on the sign-in screen and the phone is refused. (d) The tab shows the sign-in screen and no list. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): sign-in-devices.spec.ts and api/session-security.spec.ts assertions, judged against T2 (separate sessions, both valid at once) and U9 ('immediately' read as 'the next call is refused'; an open screen with no call is Q7, timed in S10). Only the operator-revoke row is checked for 'no email'. …

Where it ran: local lane A (existing Playwright tests); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S09 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane A.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: matrix (lane A).
